title: Cross-model prefix alias map for KV reuse across model variants
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem: when customers upgrade models (minor version changes, quantized variants, or family variants with compatible attention/key-value layout) we see large duplication in GPU-resident KV entries for identical prefixes. This increases GPU memory pressure, slows cold-starts, and reduces effective cache hit rate across shards. Existing dedupe work focuses on intra-model prefix fingerprinting; we need a pragmatic, version-aware layer that safely reuses compatible KV entries across model variants without risking incorrect generations or privacy leaks.

Proposal: implement a small runtime alias layer (prefix alias map) that maintains a compact mapping from (prefix-id, source-model-schema-hash) -> alias-records that point to canonical KV storage entries together with a lightweight transformation spec. The alias-record stores provenance tags, compatibility score, transform type (identity, cast-quantized, resolution-normalize, or per-layer-key-remap), and validation checksum. At request time the router queries the alias layer before materializing new KV entries. If the target model and cached canonical entry are compatible above a threshold, the runtime applies the transform path (GPU kernels or host-side translation) to bind the canonical entry into the target model's KV view instead of re-creating/reserving new GPU slab memory.

Key design constraints: 1) Safety: transformations must be verified by deterministic replay tests and checksum validation; if validation fails, fallback is to compute KV normally. 2) Isolation: mappings are tenant-scoped; cross-tenant aliasing is forbidden. 3) Performance: alias lookup + transform should not increase tail latency beyond 5% for p95 generation windows. 4) Memory savings target: reduce duplicate GPU KV allocations by at least 20% for customers with mixed-model fleets in the 30-day spike test.

Components to build: alias metadata store (compact, append-only), translation kernels (fast cast and reshape ops on GPU), compatibility scoring heuristics derived from schema hashes and tokenization invariants, runtime binding path, verification harness and E2E tests, and operational dashboards (alias hit/miss, transform latency, validation failures).

Acceptance criteria: 1) Unit tests and integration tests covering identity and quantized-cast transforms with checksum verification. 2) Benchmark showing >=20% reduction in duplicate GPU KV allocations on internal mixed-model traces with <=5% p95 latency regression. 3) Rollout plan and canary that allows safe rollback when validation failure rate >0.1% or customer error rate increases. 4) Security review completed documenting tenant-scope enforcement and auditability.

Rollout plan: implement behind runtime flag, enable for internal tenants and low-risk customers, monitor alias-hit ratio, validation-failure rate, p95 latency and token throughput per-GPU. Gradually enable for more tenants and model families after two weeks of stable metrics.

Observability: add metrics alias_lookup_{hit,miss}, alias_transform_latency_ms, alias_validation_failures, alias_memory_saved_bytes, alias_bind_fallback_count. Add per-tenant sampling traces for transform pipeline.

Documentation: runbook for disabling aliasing, description in runtime docs, and a Confluence design doc (link to: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/ALIAS-MAP-DOC) and benchmark dashboard (internal).

2025-03-11: Quick spike prototyped identity-alias binding on CPU-hosted KV; observed 18% drop in duplicate allocations on sample trace (internal/bench/mix-1).
2025-03-12: Implemented compact alias metadata layout and unit tests for tenant scoping. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3682
2025-03-13: Ported simple cast-transform kernel to GPU (fp16 <-> int8 path) and measured transform latency 0.9ms median on A100. Added preliminary metrics for alias_lookup_hit/miss.
